item.title: Oura faces lawsuit accusing it of misleading consumers about sleep-tracking accuracy
item.dc:creator: Aisha Malik
item.description: The lawsuit alleges that Oura rings are unable to measure any of the physiological signals needed to assess sleep quality or determine sleep stages.

item.title: Walmart to finally start accepting Apple Pay and Google Pay
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Are pigs flying? Walmart has finally caved on its refusal to support Apple Pay and Google Pay.

item.title: Starcloud raises $250 million for orbital data centers as launch options dry up
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: There's about to be a big fight to secure access to space.

item.title: Tesla recalls 3 million cars as part of China-wide push to stop hidden door handles
item.dc:creator: Sean O'Kane
item.description: Tesla and eight other automakers will install warning labels that help occupants identify the often hard-to-find manual door releases.

item.title: Private equity firm Apollo confirms data breach amid hacking wave targeting financial giants
item.dc:creator: Zack Whittaker
item.description: The private equity giant confirms a breach, weeks after Google researchers said hackers were targeting financial companies.

item.title: Senator asks US government watchdog to review how feds use hacking tools
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Franceschi-Bicchierai
item.description: Senator Ron Wyden sent a letter to the U.S. federal watchdog requesting a comprehensive review of how the FBI, DEA, ICE's HSI, and the Secret Service use hacking tools and spyware against Americans.

item.title: Tesla, Uber, and Waymo all get the OK to operate thousands of robotaxis in Nevada
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec
item.description: Together, these permits would allow up to 8,000 robotaxis to be deployed over the next 12 months.

item.title: AI data startup Micro1 reaches $500M gross run rate amid AI training boom
item.dc:creator: Marina Temkin
item.description: Surging demand for AI training data is driving rapid growth for the startup and its rivals.

item.title: Learn what VCs actually want, from a founder who’s raised $1B
item.dc:creator: Maggie Nye
item.description: Investors want founders who understand the financial reality of their business. Messy data, misunderstood metrics, or waiting until you’re nearly out of cash to start fundraising can cost founders leverage, valuation, and even a term sheet. In this episode of Build Mode, host Isabelle Johannessen sits down with Sasha Orloff, founder and CEO of Puzzle […]

item.title: OpenAI is gaining on Anthropic with business users, new data indicates
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: Businesses are willing to flop back and forth as each lab releases new models, volatility that should give both companies' investors pause about how "sticky" enterprise AI spending really is.

item.title: ChatGPT can now send texts for you with new Apple Messages plug-in
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: Ever wanted someone else to do your texting for you? ChatGPT is being offered up as an automated text scribe via a new Apple Messages integration.

item.title: The Enhanced Games — tech’s steroid extravaganza — didn’t pay off, as company posts $60 million loss
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: An effort to transform the world of sports through steroid use doesn't exactly seem to be bearing financial fruit.

item.title: OK, can we actually cool data centers with our pee?
item.dc:creator: Amanda Silberling
item.description: Jason Kelce joked that people should cool data centers with their pee, rather than potable water -- but his suggestion is not completely ludicrous.

item.title: Someone targeted security researchers using a fake crypto conference as a lure
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Franceschi-Bicchierai
item.description: A hacker pretending to work for a leading cryptocurrency news website targeted several cybersecurity professionals using Google Docs as a way to deliver malware.

item.title: Mark buys a castle
item.dc:creator: Dominic-Madori Davis
item.description: Mark Zuckerberg just bought a cozy abode somewhat close to Meta’s international headquarters in Ireland.

item.title: Google gives publishers a new way to fight AI-driven traffic losses
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Google is giving publishers a new button that lets readers make them a preferred source across Search, Discover, and Google News, potentially boosting their traffic as AI search sends fewer clicks to the web.

item.title: Runlayer, Rippling drop lawsuits — but the brouhaha is still a cautionary tale for founders
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: Runlayer and Rippling have dropped their lawsuits. No money was paid. Rippling celebrated by releasing a competing product.

item.title: Castelion hits $13B valuation to mass-produce hypersonic missiles
item.dc:creator: Marina Temkin
item.description: Founded in 2022, Castelion set out to manufacture hypersonic weapon systems at a lower cost and at faster speeds than traditional defense primes.

item.title: Linkdaze’s smart calendar is built to run a household, not just track a schedule
item.dc:creator: Lauren Forristal
item.description: Linkdaze's smart digital calendar stands out for not putting its features behind a paywall, including an AI meal planner tool.

item.title: Grok keeps sending gibberish responses to users
item.dc:creator: Russell Brandom
item.description: Affected users told TechCrunch they were using Grok Lite, and noticed the issues as early as Wednesday morning.
